Subject: overflow edits

Hi Marcus,

Saw that The Reel Estate Studio makes social video for estate agents in Surrey and South West London. When a few jobs land in the same week, do you ever need an extra editor?

I edit reels for a real estate firm in Goa, India. This one got about 7,000 likes: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdYG1rVMhbx/
I can work white label, so it goes out under your name, and edits come back within 48 hours.

Want me to do a free test edit on one of your clips, so you can judge?

Sahil
Sahil Jamnani, video editor, Goa, India
sahiledits.com

P.S. If this isn't for you, just reply "no" and I won't email again.


FOLLOW-UP 1 (day 3, same thread)

Hi Marcus,

The usual worry with a new editor is missed deadlines or going quiet, so try me on one edit first, free. You send the raw clips and one past reel in your style. I match your fonts, captions and music, and since I'm in India the cut is often ready by your next morning. I never contact your clients or post the work.

Worth a try?

Sahil

I'll stop here so I don't fill your inbox. If a busy week ever comes up, just reply here and I'll take a reel or two off your plate.

Sahil

questions.question: Cut the 4 spec re-cuts like this?
questions.context: Sam, Christian, Aurora, Empist. Nadia skipped.
questions.body:
4 spec re-cuts, plan before I cut. Each ~25-34 s, vertical, their own colours. No title at the start: the first word is the point.

NADIA: skipped. Her reels have text top and bottom the whole way, and she has no long video. She gets the plain short DM.

1) SAM: his own screenshot reel, re-cut (41 s -> 25 s). Both his podcasts are audio only, so this is the only footage. A closer crop hides his old captions.
- "We built a tool to scan through all of these screenshots in about six seconds. It can find places and events..." (face, then app scanning)
- small tag: Sam Levy, ex-COO of Hinge, building Rodeo
- "This weekend, I searched what to do with my son on Sunday. It reminded me that I had a gift certificate to a bowling alley." (app screens)
- "It was all just a super easy way to get out of the house." (his son bowling)
- "If you're interested, leave a comment. I'll get 100 people on this build..." / "It's free, it's easy to use, and hopefully it's useful." (face)
Cut: "Hi, I'm Sam" and the filler lines.

2) CHRISTIAN: from the Dragonfruit vlog (4K), ~28 s. A big theory, then Matt's joke.
- Christian: "This is how consumer tech evolves." / "There's human motives that are just inherent to nature." / Matt bored, chin on hand: "...we want to socialize."
- "Let's go back to the 1900s, was mail... Email became a thing... then email became social media."
- "Online dies, real life exists, too much real life, now people want to go online, and it's a cycle."
- Matt: "You lost me probably like 10 minutes ago." / Christian: "How did I lose you, bro?" / Matt: "I don't know, I just need to sit on it for a little bit." END

3) AURORA: from their Real Talk with Mercedes Bidart (Quipu), ~34 s. (Her dad story had their quote text over it the whole time, so this part instead.)
- "Let's say you have a beauty salon in a low-income neighborhood."
- "You have inventory, equipment, clients, but you can't prove your financial statements. Maybe no bank account, not registered."
- "So we capture your inventory, your equipment, your transactions, even on a digital wallet."
- "That's how we can measure not just your present and your risk, but also your potential." END

4) EMPIST: from their podcast Tech One, Two EP 9 (68 views), ~28 s.
- Nick: "My boss asked me to do this report with five different spreadsheets. I'm just going to throw it into ChatGPT. Nobody's going to know. I'm going to look so smart in front of my boss..."
- "So guess what? You just exposed your organization to huge risks: operational, financial, reputational."
- "We don't use AI in the work environment because of convenience."
- John: "We really want to look at how do we use AI responsibly, securely, and to truly drive some business value." END

New DMs (after you OK the cuts), e.g. Sam: "Sam, the chronic screenshotter reel is a great way to show Rodeo." / "I edit talking-head reels. I re-cut it with the tool in the first second and the bowling story up front." / "Want to see it?"

questions.question: Portfolio remake 03 (AI explainer, split screen like Kallaway): storyboard OK? I'm building v1 now.
questions.context: Talking footage = Jake Dawson (Creative Commons). Reply with notes in 'other' if you want changes.
questions.body:
REMAKE 03 - AI explainer, split screen (Kallaway format) - storyboard v1, 20 Nov
About 58 s, 9:16.

Footage: Jake Dawson, YouTube "How to Build Your First AI Agent" (4K).
Creative Commons, reuse allowed: we only add a credit line.
(Your own talking footage is on the hard drive, which is not plugged in.)

Layout like Kallaway: top half = a picture that shows the words, bottom half = the speaker.
A few lines = full face. Small white subtitles on the middle line, bigger ones on full-face shots.

1. 0-4 s | "Your AI is no longer a tab that you have to open." | top: browser tabs, the AI tab closes
2. 4-6 s | "It's a contact in your phone." | top: phone contacts, the "Agent" contact lights up
3. 6-10 s | "It's an AI agent that runs on its own computer in the background." | top: stock clip, a computer working at night
4. 10-12 s | "Here's the whole idea in one sentence." | full face
5. 12-17 s | "A normal AI answers you, an agent does things for you." | full-screen picture (his video has no face here): a chat answer, then the agent ticking off tasks
6. 17-19 s | "That's it. That's the whole difference." | full face, a bit closer, eyes in the same spot
7. 19-29 s | "Watch this competitor's pricing page and ping me if anything changes. Draft replies to anything routine. Remind me to follow up with anyone who went quiet." | top: phone chat with the agent, each message types in on his words, then a quick look at the result (price drop ping, drafts ready, reminder)
8. 29-38 s | "None of those are impressive on their own, but added up, they gave me back the first two hours of my day." | top: the 7-9 am block in a calendar clears, then a pile of notifications
9. 38-46 s | "Stop thinking of AI as something you talk to, start thinking of it as something you hand a job to." | top: stock, someone talking to a phone, then hands passing a folder
10. 46-48 s | "It's not chatting, it's doing." | full face, "doing" in italic
11. 48-52 s | "This stuff that used to take a developer now takes a sentence." | top: stock, a coder at screens, then one line typed and sent
12. 52-57 s | "Let me know in the comments: what's the first thing you'd hand off to an agent?" | top: comment box, a few answers pop in

Sound: his voice, quiet music, small clicks and whooshes on picture changes.
No title in the first second (your rule). Kallaway opens with a red title banner: say if you want one.

questions.context: Free CC BY footage of a US ER doctor, ~65 s
questions.body:
REMAKE 08 - Expert talking head (Doctor Mike format) - storyboard v1, 23 Nov
About 65 s, 9:16.

What the reference does (Doctor Mike, 107 s): one expert talks to camera. Small white bold
subtitles, 1-3 words, on his chest. Key lines become big 2-line text. Face zooms in and out.
Stock clips with words on top. A source page with a yellow highlighter. One blurred-face moment
with huge words. Ends on his face.

Footage: Seth Capehart MD (ER doctor), YouTube "The Longevity Lie No One Talks About" (4K, 1.5M views).
Creative Commons: free to reuse, we add a credit line. Stock clips: Pexels (free).
(Your own footage is on the hard drive, which is not plugged in.)

1. 0-8 s | "Modern medicine has gotten incredibly good at keeping people alive. It has not gotten very good
   at keeping people healthy." | his face, zoom in on "It has not". Big text: KEEPING PEOPLE HEALTHY
2. 8-16 s | "People live a long time in a very broken, unhealthy state. I'm talking about men and women..."
   | stock: old man in a hospital bed. Big text: BROKEN, UNHEALTHY STATE
3. 16-20 s | "...who aren't that old, sometimes 60s, sometimes even 50s," | his face, closer
4. 20-23 s | "who can't walk across a room without getting winded," | stock: older man out of breath
5. 23-27 s | "who fall because they're weak, not because they're unlucky," | stock: two people help a weak old man sit
6. 27-34 s | "and who come in over and over again for things that are completely predictable and sadly were
   very preventable." | his face. Big text: VERY PREVENTABLE
7. 34-37 s | "And here's a stat that should bother you." | quick zoom-blur into a close shot of his face
8. 37-47 s | "After age 30, adults lose 3 to 8% of muscle mass per decade... After 60, that accelerates even
   faster." | full-screen chart: a muscle bar shrinks at 30, 40, 50, 60; after 60 it drops faster (red)
9. 47-53 s | "Falls are one of the leading causes of injury-related death and disability in older adults."
   | a clean fact page; yellow highlighter runs over "Falls are the leading cause of injury death for
   adults 65+". Source: CDC
10. 53-56 s | "Not cancer. Not heart attacks. Falls." | page blurs, huge words one by one:
   NOT CANCER. / NOT HEART ATTACKS. / FALLS.
11. 56-65 s | "Longevity isn't about avoiding death. It's about avoiding dependence. And the earlier you
   start, the lighter the load is on everyone else." | his face. Big text: AVOIDING DEPENDENCE. Ends on him.

Sound: his voice, quiet calm music, soft whoosh on the zoom-blur, small pop on big words.
Credit line, last 3 s: Footage: Seth Capehart MD (YouTube, CC BY), edited · Stock: Pexels · Music: Mixkit
Note: his own video is blurred with text in parts 2, 8, 9-10, so those parts are covered by stock or graphics.
The falls line is checked (CDC). The 3-8% is his number (Harvard says 3-5%); we show it as his words.
